event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_prem: The Early Wake
A white wake races straight toward your ship, but no vessel leads it. In seconds, its path will cross yours exactly.
Cut across the wake
You turn too early: the wake lifts the hull and tears away rigging.
The hull lands hard, but you stay on line.
You slip between two crests without losing speed.
You use the wake's push like a perfect ramp.
Read its rhythm
You track the wrong crest and a lurch throws you against the deck.
You understand the rhythm too late to avoid every jolt.
The pattern reveals a safe gap one second before impact.
You even spot an impossible trough, as if the wake were waiting for you.
Hold course
You refuse to gamble with a phenomenon that has no visible ship. The wake comes anyway.
Let the navigator call it
The navigator calls the counter-move too late; the hull takes the crest.
The correction limits the hit without avoiding it.
The navigator finds the seam between the waves.
The maneuver turns the phenomenon to your advantage.
The Boat After Its Wake
The wake passes you. Then a tiny skiff appears behind it, moving stern-first. Its pilot waves as if nothing were unusual.
Hail the pilot
The pilot shouts that his boat is “running late behind its own wake.”
Give it room
You give him a wide berth. He thanks you for being punctual.
Demand an explanation
He sighs as if you were the hundredth person to ask the wrong question.
Tomorrow's Right of Way
The pilot raises a sign: “TOMORROW'S WAKE HAS RIGHT OF WAY.” The skiff is already fading, while its next wake forms ahead of you.
Respect the rule
You let the second wake pass. This time, the deck stays intact.
Beat tomorrow to it
You cut ahead of the forming wave and draw one last curse from the vanished pilot.
Remember the rule
You commit the absurd logic of the phenomenon to memory. It may prove useful again.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_hori: The Horizon Tax
A man behind a desk balanced on a raft blocks your way. He demands 300 Berrys in “horizon tax” before allowing you to look any farther.
Invent an exemption
Your lie collapses after two questions; he adds a “bad-faith surcharge.”
He does not believe you, but agrees to keep talking.
You quote an imaginary regulation confidently enough to make him hesitate.
He apologizes and fills out your exemption certificate himself.
Inspect his seal
You mistake a sauce stain for an official crest, and he beams.
The seal looks dubious without revealing its trick.
The “maritime seal” is an inked cup bottom.
You also spot three previous names scratched off his fake permit.
Pay 300 Berrys
He pockets the money and issues a receipt valid “until the next horizon.”
Refuse the tax
You refuse. He stamps the air in front of you with offended gravity.
The Debtor Stamp
The collector stamps the sea surface. A red mark immediately floats beside you: “HORIZON UNPAID.”
Smear the stamp
The mark dissolves under your hand and stains the collector's raft instead.
Wear the mark
You let it drift beside you. Distant travelers laugh and wave.
Stamp his desk
You turn his own stamp against the desk. The collector declares the case “administratively confused.”
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_upwa: The Upward Anchor
A rusty anchor bursts from the depths, chain stretched downward, and hooks your rail. Something beneath the sea keeps hoisting it toward the sky.
Wrench it free
The anchor wins: you wrench your shoulder and the rail splinters.
You dislodge it at the cost of a torn chunk of wood.
You lift it just enough to free the rail.
You reverse its pull and the chain shoots upward.
Cut the chain
The chain whips across the deck and hits you before snapping.
You cut it, but a link tears paint and a plank.
The chain parts cleanly away from hands and rigging.
You cut exactly as the tension reverses; nothing touches the hull.
Lever it with the shipwright
The fulcrum slips and the anchor gouges a new scar.
The rig holds just enough to avoid the worst.
The shipwright spreads the load and frees the rail.
The rig sends the entire pull back into the chain without touching the hull.
Let it pull briefly
You let the pull lift the side. The ship groans, then something rises with the chain.
The Chair on the Chain
A perfectly dry chair emerges on the chain. A sleeping fisherman is strapped into it, cap over his eyes, as if riding an elevator.
Wake the fisherman
He opens one eye, asks “surface already?”, then unhooks his chair without apologizing.
Demand repairs
He hands you two fistfuls of useless bolts, salutes, and dives back down with his chair.
Send him back down
You push the chair away. The fisherman does not even wake before vanishing below.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_floa: The Door Without a Wall
A lacquered door floats upright on the water, with no wall or raft. Three knocks sound from the other side even though you can see the sea behind it.
Open from the side
You choose the wrong angle; the door slams and catches your fingers.
You avoid the door, but not the gust behind it.
You read the door's movement and stay out of its path.
You spot a second invisible handle just before opening.
Knock back three times
You miss the rhythm; the door answers with an offended blast.
Silence lingers, then the handle slowly turns.
Three polite knocks answer yours before it opens.
The door cracks open as if inviting you personally.
Circle the door
You confirm there is nothing behind, below, or around it. The handle turns anyway.
Respect the omen
You refuse to touch the door. It opens by itself, apparently offended.
The Corridor in the Air
Beyond the door stretches a lit corridor with no building around it. A violent draft pours out, carrying hats, papers, and the smell of soup.
Slam it shut
The wind shoves you back and the door clips you.
You gain ground inch by inch before closing it.
You shut it cleanly; the corridor vanishes with the click.
You close it so fast the draft sucks its own papers back inside.
Shout “occupied!”
A distant voice answers “sorry!” and closes the door from somewhere impossible.
Peek without entering
You glimpse numbered doors running down to minus twelve before the corridor folds away.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_pred: Foam That Speaks First
Foam letters form around you. They spell exactly what you are about to say, one second before you open your mouth.
Say the opposite on purpose
The foam corrects your lie before you can finish it and makes you look foolish.
You muddle the sentence, but the foam still follows your intent.
You change your intent at the last instant and beat the foam.
You make it write a false line, then say the truth with a grin.
Think without words
The harder you avoid words, the more foam writes around you.
You earn a few seconds of silence before one letter appears.
You turn your intent into a mental image; the foam stays blank.
The foam starts drawing instead of writing, completely trapped.
Read it aloud
You let the foam lead the conversation. It eventually writes an instruction instead of a sentence.
Have the scholar test it
The test turns into an argument over definitions that the foam predicts word for word.
The phenomenon resists the first hypotheses.
The scholar isolates the exact second when the foam “reads” intent.
The test forces the foam to write two contradictory predictions.
The Predicted Hand
The foam gathers into one last sentence: “YOU WILL TAKE THE LEFT ONE.” Two identical shells float before you, one on each side.
Take the right one
The right shell dissolves into foam. The message adds: “NICE TRY.”
Take the left one
The left shell stays perfectly ordinary. The foam simply writes “THANK YOU” and vanishes.
Take neither
Both shells dive together. For one second, the foam writes nothing at all.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_banq: The Drifting Banquet
A fully set dining table glides across the sea with no vessel. A maître d' standing on a chair invites you to the “fourth course,” but forbids getting the cloth wet.
Take a seat
You sit on a chair barely afloat. The maître d' rings the service bell.
Ask the price first
He says the bill is paid “in impeccable table manners.” This clarifies nothing.
Push the table away
You push the banquet away. Every plate turns toward you like an offended face.
Have the musician toast
The toast is so theatrical that the maître d' grants you “tolerable guest” status.
The Cutlery Takes Position
At the bell, forks begin marching across the cloth. Knives surround the diners' wrists to correct their “posture.”
Dodge the cutlery
A knife bites your fingers while the maître d' records a violation.
You avoid the blades but knock a plate into the sea.
You keep your hands out of reach without touching the cloth.
You make the cutlery dance until it returns itself to place.
Follow the etiquette
You let the cutlery correct your posture. The maître d' finally approves with a one-millimeter nod.
Fold the napkin into a flag
The maître d' declares the table “diplomatic territory” and orders the knives to stand down.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_heck: The Heckling Buoy
A striped buoy starts following you against the current. With every bob it shouts a different insult in a voice that is disturbingly well informed.
Shout back louder
The buoy steals your best comeback and shouts it better than you.
You talk over each other until all dignity is gone.
You find the line that makes it stammer.
The buoy falls silent for a full second, beaten at its own game.
Find the voice source
You lean too close and the buoy screams directly into your ear.
No opening matches the voice.
A tiny shell is wedged beneath its waterline.
You also spot a second tube aimed at distant ships.
Ignore it stubbornly
You answer nothing. The buoy eventually changes tactics.
Start a musical duel
The buoy finds a brutal rhyme that sticks immediately.
The duel loops without a winner.
The musician turns the insults into an irresistible chorus.
Even the buoy joins the chorus and forgets to insult you.
The Buoy Bulletin
The buoy changes voice and announces to distant silhouettes that you carry “one hundred tons of gold, three princes, and a wanted duck.”
Silence the shell
The voice chokes underwater. The buoy keeps moving lips it does not have.
Make the lie bigger
You shout that the duck commands a fleet too. The distant silhouettes abruptly change course.
Deny everything
You spend several minutes denying the duck exists. The buoy treats this as a victory.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_cloc: The Metronome Swell
A brass metronome floats ahead of your ship. On every click, the sea rises in square steps; off-beat, it becomes perfectly flat.
Ride the beat
You miss the downbeat; the hull drops a full step of water.
You find the rhythm, but each mistake rattles the planks.
You slide the ship from one water-step to the next.
You turn the swell into a perfectly regular staircase.
Snatch the metronome
The click speeds up as you reach, and a step of water sweeps you aside.
You touch the device without getting a grip.
You catch it between clicks and the sea hesitates.
You stop the pendulum with your fingertips; the surface freezes.
Have the shipwright brace the hull
A brace fails on the wrong beat and sends the impact through the deck.
The braces limit damage without solving the rhythm.
The shipwright braces the points taking each water-step.
The hull starts flexing with the rhythm instead of fighting it.
Wait for the off-beats
You move only when the sea goes flat. Slow, humiliating, but safe.
The Metronome Boards
The metronome unfolds four tiny legs, hops onto the deck, and speeds up. Square waves begin drumming the hull.
Trap it under a bucket
The bucket shudders at every click, but the pendulum slows.
Adjust its weight
You slide the weight the wrong way and the rhythm goes wild.
The tempo drops without returning to normal.
You find a tempo that nearly cancels the swell.
You tune the pendulum to the ship's exact roll.
Kick it overboard
It bounces on the sea, offended, then its clicking suddenly slows.
The Backward Tick
The pendulum stops, then runs backward. Each tick pulls recent spray back into the sea, and deck dents creak as if unsure they should exist.
Allow three ticks
Three ticks are enough: a few superficial marks straighten before you stop the mechanism.
Stop it immediately
You stop the pendulum before the ship's own logic starts running backward too.
Throw it far
The metronome clicks away toward the horizon. The sea finally returns to ordinary rounded waves.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_invi: Invisible Customs
A perfectly straight line of spray cuts across the sea. A customs officer on a floating stool asks you to declare weapons, goods, and “contraband thoughts.”
Invent a thought manifest
He makes you recite your fake manifest backward and you contradict yourself.
He does not buy the story, but has no proof otherwise.
You declare three perfectly boring thoughts and he loses interest.
You make him fill in the category he just invented.
Challenge his jurisdiction
You cite a contradictory rule and he opens an even thicker ledger.
The argument bogs down in absurd definitions.
You prove no border can be drawn on moving spray.
You get him to inspect himself for illegal stool occupation.
Pay 200 Berrys in fees
He takes the fee and hands you a blank sheet stamped “thought inspected.”
Declare one real thought
You give him one honest thought. He records it far too seriously.
Border Visa
The officer produces an enormous stamp and says he must mark your forehead to prove “the inside was inspected.” His arm is already raised.
Dodge the stamp
The stamp catches your cheek and leaves “RECHECK” in red.
You save your forehead, not your shoulder.
You lean back just before impact and he stamps his own ledger.
You twist the stamp in his hand; his stool gets the visa.
Accept the visa
The stamp leaves only a drop of salt water. The officer looks extremely satisfied.
Stamp his ledger
You turn the move onto his papers. He frantically checks whether he is still allowed to work.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_teac: Castaways in a Teacup
A giant porcelain teacup drifts with three travelers packed inside. Their spoon serves as a mast; they beg for a tow before the remaining tea spills over.
Tow the cup
You run a line through the handle. The three castaways cheer too early.
Bring them aboard
You come alongside to bring them over one by one. The cup starts spinning around its spoon.
Give general bearings
You point them toward a traveled route. They try rowing with three saucers.
Refuse the rescue
You refuse to approach the floating crockery. The cup turns toward your wake anyway.
The Spoon Spins
The spoon starts spinning like a propeller. The cup races toward your hull while the three travelers argue over who should drop the sugar.
Catch the handle
The handle yanks you hard and the porcelain bangs the hull.
You slow the cup, but it scrapes the side.
You stop the cup within reach without a collision.
You steady the cup with one hand and the castaways with the other.
Match its spin
You take the wrong side and the cup bounces off the hull.
You limit the hit without stopping the spin.
You synchronize the ship with the spin and recover the travelers.
You use the rotation to peel the cup cleanly away from the side.
Cut every line
You release the cup before it drags anything with it. The travelers spin away, furious but intact.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_walk: Crates That Board Themselves
Six sealed crates run across the surface on tiny wooden legs. They catch your ship and start climbing the hull without invitation.
Kick them off
A crate slams your shin and two others slip past you.
You knock several away, but the smaller ones cling on.
You clear the rail before they reach the deck.
You send them back into the water in one clean chain.
Read their labels while they run
You track the wrong crate and trip into their line.
The labels shift too fast to form a sentence.
The six labels together read: “DELIVERY: NEAREST DECK.”
You also spot a tiny “return to sender” under every foot.
Have the quartermaster sort them
The crates change labels faster than they can be sorted and clog the passage.
The sorting contains the chaos without explaining the delivery.
The quartermaster lines them up by their own contradictory stamps.
They discover the exact order that makes the crates sit like dogs.
Give them a lane
You clear a lane across the deck. All six crates line up at attention.
The Crate Apologizes
The largest crate opens. Inside: a bell, an empty cushion, and a note saying only “sorry.” The other five crates bow.
Ring the bell
All six crates pivot together and run back across the sea, perfectly satisfied.
Bow back
They bow even lower, then hop overboard one by one.
Refuse delivery
You fold the note and set it back on the crate. It snaps its lid shut in offense.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_dry_: The Dry Staircase
Stone steps rise from the water and climb three meters into empty air, perfectly dry. Footprints appear on the top step and descend toward you.
Climb halfway
You climb high enough to confirm the empty air. The footprints keep descending through your feet.
Wait at the bottom
You wait for the invisible thing at the bottom. The final footprint stops right in front of you.
Splash the steps
The water vanishes the instant it hits the stone. An invisible voice sighs above you.
Keep your distance
You move away. The staircase slides across the sea to stay exactly within speaking range.
The Passenger Without a Body
A wet coat takes shape around nothing on the last step. A voice from the collar politely asks, “Is this the seventh floor?”
Say “sea level”
The coat groans, climbs two steps, and vanishes. The staircase follows.
Ask where it came from
The voice answers “minus eleven” like someone who has missed another connection.
Point downward
The coat thanks you and walks straight through the surface without using the stairs.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_pape: The Paperwork Current
Hundreds of waterproof forms surround your route. Every time a stamp slams itself onto a sheet, the current immediately changes direction.
Forge a redirect order
You tick two incompatible boxes; the current spins in place and throws you around.
The form is rejected for lacking a prerequisite form.
You produce an order coherent enough to turn the papers.
You find the hidden “absolute priority” box in the margin.
Catch the flying stamp
The stamp smacks your fingers and validates your own failure.
You touch it without holding on.
You catch it between two forms and the current hesitates.
You stamp three forms before it can escape.
Read the fine print
You follow a note that refers back to itself and lose track of the current.
The clauses mostly describe other clauses.
One line says unsigned forms must give way.
You spot an expiration date that has already passed on the entire batch.
Have the scholar draft an appeal
The appeal cites a nonexistent annex and triggers a shower of extra forms.
The filing is “received but not processed.”
The scholar produces an objection the current accepts.
The wording forces the forms to audit one another.
Appeal in Triplicate
Three giant sheets rise before you: “APPEAL,” “APPEAL OF APPEAL,” and “PROOF YOU APPEALED.” The current waits for their order.
Stack them in order
The three forms stamp themselves and file away. The current finally relaxes.
Tear the appeal of appeal
The two remaining sheets declare each other incomplete and chase one another away.
Sign nothing
Without a signature, the system no longer knows whom to punish. The forms drift toward another administrative emergency.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_earl: The Early Shadow
A lone rower approaches in a small craft. His shadow across the water waves, grimaces, and points several seconds before he makes each gesture.
Copy the shadow
You copy each gesture before the rower does. He stops, deeply disturbed that you are “cheating.”
Talk to the rower
You ask whether he knows about his shadow. It is already nodding while he says no.
Watch only the shadow
You ignore the man and follow his double. The shadow eventually signals you to look behind.
Keep your distance
You stay far away. The shadow stretches anyway until it nearly reaches you.
The Gesture He Never Made
The shadow suddenly points behind you, then mimes pulling a rope. The rower keeps both hands on his oars and swears he planned nothing.
Read the warning
You read the gesture too late and end up tangled in a floating line.
You understand there is danger without locating it.
The gesture makes you spot a floating line passing behind you.
You also realize the shadow is warning you, not its owner.
Thank the shadow
You salute the black silhouette directly. It bows; the rower stares at his own shadow in horror.
Warn the rower
You describe the gesture. He immediately starts rowing opposite his own shadow.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_sile: The Silent Bell
An enormous bronze bell floats upside down. Whenever its clapper moves without making a sound, ropes and loose objects jump a meter toward it.
Steer out of its pull
You turn during a silent “strike” and the pull heels the ship hard.
You gain distance, but the rigging takes another wrench.
You place the hull in the dead angle between two pulls.
You use one pull to accelerate out of the zone.
Lash everything down
A loose crate hits you before you can catch it.
You secure the essentials, not the smaller pieces.
You secure the dangerous objects before the next silent strike.
You turn every loose line into a useful restraint.
Have the musician count the rhythm
The musician anticipates a strike that never comes and the whole maneuver starts early.
There is a rhythm, but it regularly skips a bar.
The musician finds the exact silence between two pulls.
They call every silent strike before the clapper even moves.
Kill your speed
You let the ship drift between pulls. The bell comes closer instead of moving away.
The Sand Rises
The bell rights itself beside the hull. Dry sand pours upward from inside it, and every grain lifts something on deck a few centimeters toward the sky.
Hook the bell rim
You hold it long enough for the sand to narrow into one column.
Rig counterweights
Your balance is wrong; several objects rise and slam back down.
The rig reduces the pull without canceling it.
You spread the weight and stabilize the deck.
You even force the bell to tilt under its own pull.
Strike the bell
This time a real note rings out. All the pull stops at once.
Everything Drops
The silence breaks. Every lifted object loses its pull at once and drops toward the deck as the bell begins to sink.
Catch the falling gear
You save one and take two others on the shoulder.
You avoid the heaviest, but not all the damage.
You catch the dangerous pieces before they hit the deck.
You turn the mass drop into almost elegant stowage.
Take cover
You protect people instead of gear. A few impacts scar the deck.
Watch the bell sink
The bell vanishes without a bubble. The last grain of sand falls upward.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_bott: A merchant standing on a plank displays jars containing tiny moving horizons. He offers to show you “a better sea” for 150 Berrys, with no guarantee.
Inside the jar, you see your own face looking into another jar. The merchant refuses refunds.
The reflections never match the current sky. You do spot the trick: no two jars show the same second.
The merchant shouts that you insult the art of portable horizons. Nearby travelers stare.
You refuse the offer. The merchant pockets twenty sunsets in his coat and drifts away.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_one_: A man on stilts crosses the sea behind six tiny paper flags. He beats a drum and demands right of way for “the grand annual parade,” of which he is the only participant.
He bows so low one stilt nearly slips. He marches on convinced he had a historic audience.
You join for a few bars. The flags immediately name you “foreign delegation.”
He produces rules rolled inside his drum: every article is signed by himself.
He declares your whistle “official opposition” and doubles the drum volume.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_dry_: The Dry Hole in the Sea
A perfect circle of sea vanishes ahead of the bow, replaced by open air several meters deep. Fish hang around the rim as if they forgot to fall.
Turn before the edge
You turn too late; the bow drops into the gap and hits the far wall of water.
The hull bites the edge of the phenomenon before pulling free.
You swing the ship around just before the missing-water edge.
You use the rim current to accelerate the turn.
Cross on momentum
Momentum fails: the hull drops, slams into the water wall, and bucks upward.
You clear the gap, but the exit impact crushes planks.
The ship crosses the dry circle and lands in water on the far side.
The hull hangs in open air for a full second before an almost clean landing.
Let the helmsman take the edge
The helmsman misreads the curve and the bow clips the dry edge.
The maneuver scrapes the phenomenon without falling in.
The helmsman follows the circle's rim to clear water.
The line is so clean the suspended fish do not even move.
Back away carefully
You give up the crossing and back away until the sea is continuous again. The detour mostly costs pride.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_sea_: A courier standing on a giant envelope glides up to you. He asks for a signature on a parcel addressed exactly to “the sea beneath your feet.”
You sign. The courier drops the parcel into the water; bubbles immediately spell a readable “THANK YOU.”
The courier sighs, writes “recipient uncooperative,” and glides away on his envelope.
The parcel sinks. One second later, bubbles spell the false name perfectly.
Ask the sea for a receipt
The courier falls silent. A wave still leaves a neat square of foam at your feet.
event.active_generic_sea_05_strange_rope: A thick rope hangs vertically from an empty sky and dips into the sea. A traveler climbs down, stops beside you, and asks, “Is this floor seven?”
The traveler counts on his fingers, swears softly, and starts climbing back into the empty sky.
He answers “mostly stairs,” then refuses to explain why he chose the rope.
The rope stays perfectly vertical despite your pull. You are the one who slides a step toward it.
The traveler thanks you and climbs below the surface without getting wet. The rope then retracts into the sky.
